decisions.reason: The Definition supplies finite-channel propensity data and the finite local operator Q, not a globally existing E-valued jump process. The quadratic pure-birth example satisfies these data and can explode, without contradicting any asserted existence or nonexplosion conclusion; no post-explosion convention is needed to define Q.

The explicit input-law justification omitted the theorem that Lebesgue measure is a measure: the definition explicitly defers that fact, and the box theorem gives interval masses. The complete-measure theorem already exists in the supplier closure and assumes exactly the declared Countable Choice, so this is an attribution defect rather than a false simulation law.

The Definition correctly specifies independent uniform inputs but attributes their probability-space status only to the restricted-set-function definition and interval-volume theorem. Add the complete-measure supplier explicitly; its Countable Choice hypothesis is already declared, and the missing theorem is in the existing dependency closure.

At a supplied threshold firing exactly at T, the original >= branch omits the event although Y counts thresholds with <=. This contradicts the unqualified pathwise identity, but lies in a null event under the required continuous input laws. The separate finite-state correctness theorem already exists; absence of a proof inside an algorithm is not itself a defect.

F3 omits an explicit complete-measure citation when constructing the unit-uniform probability factor. That theorem is available under the already declared Countable Choice. The stopped finite-state Lyapunov argument itself proves the intended nonexplosion estimate; the defect is incomplete supplier attribution, with a bounded-convergence passage also made explicit.

The input is an independent Exp(1) stream, not an arbitrary positive sequence, and this procedure makes no universal deterministic termination claim. Its separate exact-marginals theorem proves that the candidate count on [0,T] is Poisson(MT), hence finite almost surely; the cited thinning construction supplies the same bound. Summable positive streams below MT are a null event, so the proposed example does not refute this randomized procedure.

The original Statement omitted a common initial state x0 in E, allowing an empty E and an undefined rate maximum. Independently, its unqualified claim for both algorithm outputs fails at finite event budget B=0: on E={0,1} with death rate one from 1, the returned time-zero prefix is not the full path on [0,1], which reaches zero with probability 1-exp(-1). This is a logic defect in the quantified path-law claim.

A1 attributes probability laws directly to Countable Choice, whose Definition only states a selection principle. The input-law existence results of the algorithm and thinning theorem use that axiom; the axiom is not their conclusion. The marginal argument is sound, but step 1.1 also needs an explicit M_j=0 branch to avoid the displayed division by zero.

The example invokes the finite-state exactness theorem as F2 without carrying its explicit Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses. Consequently the cited interface does not justify the path-law and reaction-count conclusions as written; this is an omitted prerequisite-assumption defect. Its full-path assertion also needs the supplier theorem unlimited-budget qualification.

F3 and F4 invoke exact-marginal and thinning theorems whose Statements explicitly assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, but neither assumption appeared in the example. The supplied interfaces therefore fail to license the asserted path and first-event laws; this is an omitted prerequisite-assumption defect.

The reported auxiliary-status defect is real: if W>=T the direct call returns horizon, so absorbed requires W<T in an unlimited-budget call. Also F2 uses the finite-state exactness theorem without its Countable Choice and Dependent Choice assumptions, as in the other two examples; this missing prerequisite premise is the fatal dependency-citation defect. The absorbing-state and survival conclusions themselves have the expected values.

Checked the global envelope, zero-envelope branch, rejection partition, null endpoint marks and candidate-budget convention. Added the complete-measure dependency and precise measure-plus-unit-mass construction. Checked lambda=0 before budget, zero-budget prefixes, strict cumulative mark intervals and U=1 fallback, admissible active poststates, finite rates and independent event inputs. The simulation procedure is unchanged; this repairs the input-law citation only.

Changed the horizon test to > so the right-continuous endpoint event is recorded. Restricted the random-time-change output identity to the returned interval and stated its almost-sure scope, covering null simultaneous ties and incomplete finite-budget prefixes. Linked the existing correctness theorem with justified_by. Checked threshold updates, inactive clocks, absorption and the endpoint return. Full-horizon law remains an unlimited-budget assertion. Re-examined the later repaired correctness-theorem Statement: fixed x0 and unlimited full-horizon budgets, together with its finite-budget prefix law, establish exactly this returned-interval output contract. Recorded a fresh context only after that effect review.

Added the complete-measure dependency and F3 citation, and bounded convergence in F5 for the uniformly bounded stopped-path Riemann sums. Kept the Statement unchanged. Checked finite sublevels and one-step exits, the factorial event bound, explicit residual-history kernels, stopped drift identity, iterated Gronwall estimate, exit probability bound V(x0)exp(cT)/n and the countable-time conclusion. Conditional means are computed as explicit stream kernels, without invoking an abstract conditional-expectation existence theorem or full AC.

Left the algorithm unchanged. Checked finite per-channel envelopes, mark-block partition, nested coordinate acceptance intervals, null endpoint marks, zero M and finite-budget prefix semantics. For M>0 its candidate gaps have joint exponential density; the thinning supplier and exact-marginals theorem give finite candidate count almost surely. The common and residual intervals have lengths min(aX,aY)/M and positive differences/M, so each coordinate retains its own rates. Almost-sure termination does not assert termination on every null input realization.

Fixed x0 in E, so E is nonempty, and explicitly bound full-horizon equality to unlimited reaction-event budgets while retaining the exact finite-budget prefix claim. The event-kernel proof, exponential residual calculation, finite Poisson domination, generator derivative and expected reaction-count bound are unchanged in substance. Added the prefix stopping argument and the null deterministic-horizon event argument in step 4.1. No full AC is added; the existing Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses suffice.

Rephrased A1 to identify the axiom as an assumption of the existing input-law existence results, and treated zero per-channel envelopes by omitting their empty blocks before dividing. Statement unchanged. Checked coordinate acceptance sets depend only on their own state, are disjoint across channel labels and product-measurable, so generalized thinning proves both marginals; interval intersections and differences give the shared/residual rates, and the candidate Poisson mean MT proves almost-sure finite termination.

Added the two choice assumptions to the Statement and Given, their definition dependencies, and the accurate F2 hypotheses. Specified unlimited event budget for full-horizon output. Checked the six boundary propensities and admissible poststates, constant total rate two, Exp(2) first holding time with equally likely channel from state 1, the three generator rows and EN(T)<=2T. Initial state 1 satisfies the repaired supplier interface.

Added Countable Choice and Dependent Choice to the Statement and Given, their dependency definitions, and F3/F4. Made the already intended unlimited budget explicit in the Statement and distinguished the uncensored Exp(3) first accepted paired event from finite-horizon output. Verified boundary-disabled channels, M_birth=2, M_death=4, candidate rate six, three disjoint portions of length 1/6 at (1,1), their updates and equal probabilities, and coordinate-specific acceptance for the marginal theorem.

Added exactly the supplier choice assumptions and their definition dependencies to the Statement/Given/F2. Qualified F3 by reaching its zero-propensity test before T, and replaced the unqualified absorbed-status sentence by the W<T versus W>=T cases in step 2.1. Verified the sole active poststate, the unit exponential holding law, both state probabilities for all t>=0 and the generator entries Qf(1)=f(0)-f(1), Qf(0)=0. The underlying process claim is preserved; finite-horizon output is distinguished explicitly.
